correctness.rationale: Full proof reduces the exact entropy optimizer to an interior scalar log-odds equation, differentiates it, proves strictly convex reciprocal curvature with unique minimizer, and supplies matching checkerboard perturbations. Row/column harmonic-mean equality conditions and sign of the reciprocal-curvature derivative at independence prove rigidity and association. A standalone checker passed 9,675 supplementary assertions, which do not substitute for analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The primary full-text comparisons establish general entropic stability and implicit Sinkhorn gradients, but neither states the sharp fixed-marginal binary maximum-entry modulus, equality rigidity and association sign. A published binary sweep contraction result is about a different map, not a stronger bound for input-score perturbations. Priority remains provisional because exact binary-contingency literature is extensive.
residual_risks: Equivalent optimizations may already be known in binary log-linear, contingency-table and matrix-scaling sensitivity literature not surfaced by targeted searches.
Eckstein–Nutz 2021 arXiv work was inspected at abstract level, not by full-text theorem comparison.
Published generic implicit differentiation mathematically entails the pointwise rank-one derivative; originality resides only in globally optimizing it and the balance/association classification.

value.rationale: The exact global sensitivity of binary entropy transport under arbitrary kernel contrast is a natural sharp stability invariant for an important nonlinear coupling map. The result identifies precisely when an intuitively simple variance bound is achieved and how marginal imbalance forces worst sensitivity away from independence. These nontrivial structural conditions provide a robust benchmark; no larger-table generalization is claimed.
